items.summary: Reset token comes from Math.random(), is stored in plain text, has no expiry and nothing invalidates it after use. It is also never emailed, so the flow is incomplete.
items.fix: Generate 32 bytes with crypto.randomBytes, store only a SHA-256 hash with an expiry of 30-60 minutes, delete it on use and on password change.

items.summary: Passwords are hashed with unsalted MD5, which is cracked at billions of guesses per second.
items.fix: Use argon2id or bcrypt via a maintained library, and rehash existing users on their next login.

items.summary: /login, /signup and /forgot have no rate limiting. Searched: rate-limit|limiter|throttle across the repo, no hits.
items.fix: Add express-rate-limit backed by Redis (per IP and per email) on all auth routes.

items.summary: The 'token' returned by /login is the raw user id: it never expires and cannot be revoked, and it can be guessed.
items.fix: Issue signed, expiring session tokens or use a hosted auth provider. This is an auth rewrite, so ask an experienced engineer to review it.
